title: U.S. House · Arizona's 6th District
area: Southeastern Arizona: all of Cochise, Graham and Greenlee counties, plus part of Pima County including Tucson's eastern and southeastern suburbs (Sierra Vista, Sahuarita area).

context.text: Ballotpedia identified this race as a battleground. Ciscomani won re-election 50.7%-49.2% in 2022 and 50.0%-47.5% in 2024; Donald Trump carried the district 49.8%-49.1% in 2024. As of July 2026 election forecasters rated the general election Toss-up to Lean Democratic, and Ciscomani had raised $6.17 million to Mendoza's $7.35 million.

summary.text: Juan Ciscomani is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Arizona's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. Born in Mexico and raised in Tucson, he worked at the University of Arizona and the Tucson Hispanic Chamber of Commerce and was a senior advisor to Gov. Doug Ducey before running for Congress. He serves on the Appropriations and Veterans' Affairs committees and is seeking a third term in a district Ballotpedia calls a battleground.

background.text: Born in Mexico; according to his Ballotpedia survey, he moved to Tucson, Arizona, with his parents at age 5. His official biography says his father worked as a bus driver.

Graduated from Rincon High School in Tucson, earned an associate degree from Pima Community College, and a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona in 2005; says he was the first member of his family to graduate from college.
Worked for the University of Arizona and as membership director and vice president of outreach for the Tucson Hispanic Chamber of Commerce.

Joined Arizona Governor Doug Ducey's administration as a senior advisor and served as vice chair of the Arizona-Mexico Commission, focusing on international trade, border security and economic development.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2022, defeating Kirsten Engel 50.7 percent to 49.2 percent; his official biography says he is the first naturalized American citizen from Mexico elected to the U.S. House from Arizona.
Re-elected in 2024 over Kirsten Engel, 50.0 percent to 47.5 percent.

Committee assignments for 2025-2026: Appropriations (including the Homeland Security subcommittee, where he is vice chair, and the National Security, Department of State and Related Programs subcommittee) and Veterans' Affairs.

His official biography says the Center for Effective Lawmaking and the Lugar Center and Georgetown's McCourt School Bipartisan Index named him the most bipartisan member of Arizona's House delegation during his first term.
According to his official biography, he lives in Tucson with his wife, Laura, and their six children, and coaches a 5th- and 6th-grade flag football team.

priorities.text: Securing the border while making the legal immigration process faster and more workable, saying his own family's citizenship process took over a decade.
Reducing federal government spending, which he says has contributed to inflation in housing, groceries and other costs.
Addressing water conservation in Arizona through what he calls bipartisan effort.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (2025-2026), as vice chair of the Homeland Security Subcommittee and a member of the National Security, Department of State and Related Programs Subcommittee.
Serves on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (2025-2026), on the Economic Opportunity and Oversight and Investigations subcommittees.

candidates.name: JoAnna Mendoza

summary.text: JoAnna Mendoza is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Juan Ciscomani in Arizona's 6th Congressional District. A 20-year veteran of the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps, she later worked as a nonprofit leader, veterans' outreach coordinator and congressional staffer, and ran for the Arizona Senate in 2020. According to her Ballotpedia survey, she is running on lowering costs, protecting Social Security and strengthening the health care system.

background.text: Born in Florence, Arizona. Says her family relied on Medicaid while she was growing up and that her life has been shaped by the working families of Pinal County.

Served in the U.S. Navy from 1994 to 1997 and the U.S. Marine Corps from 1998 to 2016, including two tours in Iraq and one in Afghanistan; says she enlisted at 17 and served as a Marine Corps Drill Instructor.

Earned a bachelor's degree from American Military University in 2013, a graduate degree from Grand Canyon University in 2019 (a master's in leadership, per her survey), and a graduate degree from Arizona State University.
Worked as a veterans outreach coordinator for Pima Community College, a program manager at A Place Called Home, and a veteran services representative for U.S. Rep. Tom O'Halleran (D).
Describes herself as a single mother, nonprofit leader, veteran advocate and congressional staffer.
Won the Democratic primary for Arizona State Senate District 11 in 2020 with 57.4 percent, then lost the general election to incumbent Vince Leach (R), 54.4 percent to 45.6 percent.
Advanced unopposed from the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary for Arizona's 6th District.

priorities.text: Says she is committed to improving public education, increasing access to affordable healthcare, and preserving Arizona's natural environment and water resources.
Says she wants to ensure veterans, service members and their families get needed support.
Describes a focus on community access and engagement, working across the aisle, and action-oriented, implementable solutions.

positions.summary: Says she is committed to increasing access to affordable healthcare.
positions.quote: I am committed to improving our public education system, increasing access to affordable healthcare, and preserving our natural environment and scarce water resources.

candidates.researchNotes: Her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers on file (cited above) were submitted in 2020 for a state Senate race, not this 2026 congressional race; content is used only where it reflects durable personal background and stated values, not district-specific positions.

candidates.name: Gary Swing
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Green Party primary as a write-in candidate.

summary.text: Gary Swing is the Green Party candidate on the general-election ballot for Arizona's 6th Congressional District. Originally from New Jersey and educated in political science at the University of Colorado, he has worked as a cultural events promoter, postal carrier and grocery produce receiver. By his own account he has appeared on ballots in Arizona and Colorado as an alternative-party candidate since 1996, and his survey answers emphasize nonviolence, reduced military spending and proportional representation.

background.text: Born in Willingboro, New Jersey; earned a high school diploma from Friends School in Mullica Hill, a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Colorado Boulder (1991) and a master's degree in political science from the University of Colorado Denver (1999).

Career experience includes work as a cultural events promoter (about twenty years, per his survey), a U.S. postal carrier, a produce receiver for Whole Foods, and a public policy research assistant at the University of Colorado Denver's Graduate School of Public Affairs.

Says he has been on the ballot thirteen times as an alternative-party candidate since 1996, including seven times with the Green Party and three times with the Unity Party of Colorado, in both Colorado and Arizona. He ran in Colorado's 1st District in 2012, and says he received 138,634 votes (5.5 percent) as a Green candidate for U.S. Senate in Arizona.

Former co-chair of the Colorado Coalition for Fair and Open Elections and former spokesperson for the election-reform group Best Democracy; says he lobbied in 2019 against a bill raising petition signature requirements for independent candidates.
Describes himself as a lifelong pacifist and a long-distance backpacker who has hiked the Appalachian and Pacific Crest trails.

priorities.text: Says the U.S. should cut the military budget by 90%, close foreign bases, end foreign military aid and intervention, and abolish nuclear weapons.
Wants to replace the current system of government with a unicameral Congress elected by proportional representation and a parliamentary system, abolishing the U.S. Senate and Electoral College.
Supports Medicare for all, a universal basic income, and a 'steady state' economy built around environmental sustainability, including transition away from fossil fuels and nuclear energy.

positions.summary: Opposes continued U.S. military aid to Israel and says Israel has committed genocide against Gaza; supports war crimes tribunals and reparations.
positions.quote: Israel has committed genocide against Gaza. I support war crimes tribunals, reparations to the people of Gaza, and nonviolent conflict resolution.

positions.summary: Supports federal legislation to secure abortion rights.
positions.quote: Pass federal legislation to secure abortion rights.

positions.summary: Supports a single-payer healthcare system covering everyone.
Opposes immigration enforcement expansion; wants to abolish ICE, oppose a border wall, and allow freedom of migration.
positions.quote: Abolish ICE. Support "fair trade" policies and freedom of migration. No border wall.

positions.summary: Supports transitioning away from fossil fuels and nuclear energy to renewable energy sources as part of a sustainable, steady-state economy.
positions.quote: Transition away from fossil fuels and nuclear energy to renewable energy sources. Protect public lands.

candidates.researchNotes: Completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; no campaign finance activity or additional news coverage of this 2026 race found.

candidates.name: Jereme Peters

summary.text: Jereme Peters is the Libertarian Party candidate on the general-election ballot for Arizona's 6th Congressional District. He advanced from the Libertarian primary on July 21, 2026. No biography or platform for him was found in the sources reviewed.

candidates.researchNotes: Checked https://ballotpedia.org/Jereme_Peters (September 2026): no biography, and Peters has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. No campaign website or news coverage found beyond his listing as a candidate and FEC filer ($10,500 raised).

candidates.name: Michael Dorland

summary.text: Michael Dorland is an independent write-in candidate on the general-election ballot for Arizona's 6th Congressional District who has worked in information technology. He describes a working-class background that included restaurant, retail and field-service jobs and small-business ownership. His campaign says it accepts no donations or party backing, and his survey answers emphasize anti-corruption measures and technology oversight.

background.text: Grew up in rural South Dakota; says his family lost their house and business when he was young, and that he was briefly homeless as an adult.

Work history includes dishwasher and kitchen manager, about four years in retail at K-Mart and Walmart, two years as a Dell field service technician in southern Arizona (Sierra Vista, Benson, Douglas), and owner of a comic store and other small businesses.
Says he has worked with computers since 1980 with a special focus on AI; Ballotpedia lists his career experience as an information technology professional.
Says he lost his house in 2008, largely due to medical debt, while raising two young children, and that he lives with managed mental illness.
Describes himself as an independent write-in running on his own money, saying he has spent under $200 and takes no donations.

priorities.text: Says he is self-funded, taking no campaign donations and posting every expenditure publicly.
Wants stronger anti-corruption rules in Congress, including banning congressional stock trading and closing the revolving door to lobbying.
Calls for transparency on the water and power costs of AI data centers and safety testing of AI systems before they scale.

candidates.researchNotes: Completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey with an extensive biography and platform, but his answers do not directly address any of the 15 tracked issue statements (his immigration views are described as being on his campaign website, which was not independently fetched). No FEC financial activity reported as of this filing period.
